nodes.label: Web Accessibility
nodes.rationale: Accessibility and SEO are not competing priorities; both make a site clearer and easier to navigate, so improving one naturally helps the other.

nodes.label: SEO
nodes.rationale: Search optimization usually improves the experience for real people; search engines reward clarity, structure, and usability that accessibility also requires.

nodes.label: Semantic HTML
nodes.rationale: Use elements that describe content (header, nav, main, footer) instead of generic divs so screen readers and search engines can understand page structure; one h1 per page with ordered headings.

nodes.label: ARIA Roles and Labels
nodes.rationale: Use ARIA only when standard HTML falls short; overusing roles creates more problems than it solves. Prefer WAI-ARIA practices for complex UI like modals and tabs.

nodes.label: Mobile-First Design
nodes.rationale: Google indexes the mobile version first; accessibility also means supporting different devices and input methods; tap targets at least 44x44px.

nodes.label: useState
nodes.rationale: Analogized to coffee powder and hot water: simple, local, foundational state that everything else builds on.

nodes.label: useEffect
nodes.rationale: Analogized to brewing: handles timing and side effects so things react at the right moment; cannot be rushed.

nodes.label: Custom Hooks
nodes.rationale: Analogized to a signature coffee recipe: personal reusable logic that makes behavior just how you like it.

nodes.label: useContext
nodes.rationale: Analogized to a shared kitchen coffee jar: shared values accessible without prop drilling.

nodes.label: Coffee Equals React Hooks Metaphor
nodes.rationale: Simple familiar ingredients plus patient process yield something smooth and reusable—same beauty as clean React hooks code.

nodes.label: Dog-Friendly Third Place
nodes.rationale: Dream of a real hangout for people and dogs—not a quick stop—combining boarding, a small park, and a café where both can share space.

nodes.label: Curiosity Instead of Fear
nodes.rationale: Dogs stayed calm with fearless curious kids but bark at tense guests; we often react to what we think others might do rather than who they are—approaching with curiosity could calm interactions.

nodes.label: Markdown-Powered Next.js Blog
nodes.rationale: Chose Markdown files + Next.js/TypeScript over headless CMS, database, or Notion backend for speed, type safety, zero monthly cost, and fit with existing workflow.

nodes.label: Build-Time Markdown Parsing
nodes.rationale: Next.js parses markdown at build time, generates pages, and handles SEO metadata for instant loads and full control.

nodes.label: Wix Velo
nodes.rationale: Used Velo when editor/widgets were not enough—treat Wix as hosted front-end with built-in database rather than pure drag-and-drop.

nodes.label: Wix CMS Collections
nodes.rationale: Put shared content in collections even for a single settings row to avoid stale duplicated headlines; design collections before polishing layouts.

nodes.label: Wix Automations
nodes.rationale: Wire form submits through Automations for email/Slack-style flows; push weird branches needing transformation into Velo instead of being a human cron job.

nodes.label: Bind vs Code Rule of Thumb
nodes.rationale: Bind when one collection maps to one repeater; drop into onReady/wix-data code when shaping, filtering, or combining data.

nodes.label: Minimal Text-Only Logo Design
nodes.rationale: Brand identity is conveyed solely through a lowercase wordmark with no icons, slogans, or secondary graphics, relying on typography and soft contrast for a quiet, modern presence.

nodes.label: Sleek Aesthetics Over Readability Trade-off
nodes.rationale: Low-contrast light gray text is framed as the result of prioritizing a sleek look over readability, causing eye strain and excluding people with visual impairments, older readers, and users in sunlight.

nodes.label: JavaScript Logo
nodes.rationale: Official-style JS brand mark: edge-to-edge yellow square (#F0DB4F) with dark charcoal (#323330) JS letterforms; portfolio tech-stack identity icon.

nodes.label: Dark-Background Logo Treatment
nodes.rationale: White path fills plus a single green accent read clearly on dark UI chrome; compact 100×24 viewBox suits nav/header placement.

nodes.label: Sass Logo
nodes.rationale: Official Sass brand mark: a single calligraphic S script glyph filled in brand pink (#CB6699) on a transparent field; used as a portfolio tech-stack identity icon for the Sass CSS preprocessor.

nodes.label: Socket.IO Logo
nodes.rationale: Official-style Socket.IO brand mark: circular ring badge with a double zigzag signal motif in near-black (#010101) on a 128×128 viewBox; portfolio tech-stack identity icon for real-time WebSocket messaging.
